chunks: Ibn Fazzal, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Zahaar does not occur except upon the similar place of the divorce.

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zahaar: A form of divorce in Islamic law where a husband declares his wife to be like his mother's back, making intercourse forbidden until expiation is made.
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ: Mawdi': Place, location, or specific part.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Zahaar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) clarifies that for Zahaar to be legally binding, the body part likened to the mother must correspond to the specific locus of divorce (Talaq), reflecting the juristic principle of precise analogical correspondence. This ruling, recorded in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on textual specificity in marital jurisprudence, distinguishing it from broader interpretations found in other schools. It highlights the importance of intent and linguistic precision in establishing the legal consequences of this unique form of marital separation.
